title: Curtain-slash and rear-door intrusion alert for curtainsiders parked overnight at truck stops and lay-bys
problem: Gangs slash the curtains of parked curtainsider trailers at service areas and lay-bys overnight and steal high-value pallets (TVs, alcohol, tyres, toiletries) while the driver sleeps in the cab; the theft is found in the morning. Load loss is ~£10k-£100k per incident, plus goods-in-transit (GIT) insurance excess (~£1k-£5k), a premium rise, and a customer who may move the contract.
who_suffers: HGV drivers taking statutory rest in the cab; transport managers handling claims and customers
buyer: Transport Manager / Operations Director of an SME haulier (operator-licence holder)
industry: UK general haulage of palletised consumer goods on curtainsider trailers
current_workaround: Paying ~£25-£35/night for secure truck parks when spaces exist, contract and GIT 'unattended vehicle' parking rules, TAPA TSR alarms on tier-1 fleets only, drivers' visual checks, reporting to police/NaVCIS after the event.
sensor_concept: Battery module on the trailer: accelerometer/vibration plus capacitive or conductive-thread sensing on the curtain and buckles, and a rear-door reed switch; LTE-M/NB-IoT with GNSS; BLE siren in the cab plus push alert to driver and office; time-stamped incident log for the GIT insurer and police.
notes: Expect strong c1 (high load value), c4 (GIT unattended-vehicle conditions, TAPA TSR), c6 (GIT brokers/insurers and telematics resellers), c10 (NaVCIS data, trade press, driver forums); c2 per-fleet frequency is the risk.

title: Tail-lift battery and hydraulic failures strand multi-drop delivery rounds; LOLER exams lack usage data
problem: A tail-lift fails mid-round (flat dedicated battery, broken charging link, hydraulic leak), so the remaining drops can't be unloaded. Each failure costs a mobile engineer callout or recovery (~£300-£600), failed deliveries, rebooking and penalties from retail clients, and it recurs several times a year per fleet. LOLER also requires a thorough examination of every tail-lift every 6 months.
who_suffers: Delivery drivers and two-person crews; fleet engineers; customer service teams rebooking deliveries
buyer: Fleet Engineer / Workshop Manager of a home-delivery, builders-merchant or drinks-wholesale fleet
industry: 7.5-26t tail-lift-equipped delivery fleets (white goods/furniture home delivery, builders merchants, beverage wholesale)
current_workaround: Driver daily walkaround of the tail-lift, reactive callouts to tail-lift service agents, 6-monthly LOLER thorough examination by engineering surveyors, swapping batteries after failure.
sensor_concept: Clip-on module at the tail-lift power pack: battery voltage, charge current (Hall sensor), motor-run cycle counter and hydraulic pressure transducer; LTE-M; alerts on low battery or charging fault before the round leaves; cycle and overload logs for the LOLER examiner and service agent.
notes: Expect strong c2 (daily use, frequent failures), c4 (LOLER 1998 6-monthly exam, PUWER), c6 (tail-lift service agent networks and LOLER inspectors already visit), c8 (cheap sensors); c1 per incident is modest, so it needs fleet-level aggregation.

title: Small frozen-food and ice-cream distributors lack the transport temperature records quick-frozen food law requires
problem: Quick-frozen food rules require transport to have temperature recording instruments and records kept (~1 year). Small ice-cream and frozen wholesale distributors running converted vans rely on cab displays and paper sheets, which leads to customer audit and EHO findings. A fridge-unit failure mid-round can write off a van load (~£3k-£10k) with no evidence of when it started.
who_suffers: Drivers; depot owner facing rejected deliveries and claims
buyer: Owner / Transport Manager of an independent frozen-food or ice-cream wholesale distributor
industry: Independent frozen-food, ice-cream and catering wholesale distributors running 3.5-7.5t refrigerated vans
current_workaround: Driver reads the cab display, handwritten temperature sheets per drop or thermal-printer tickets, annual service by a refrigeration agent, customers' goods-in probe checks.
sensor_concept: Air temperature probes per compartment plus door switch; LTE-M with GNSS; continuous log meeting the record-retention duty; alerts on rising temperature or door left open; per-drop PDF trip record; fault view for the refrigeration service agent.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Quick-frozen Foodstuffs Regs / Reg (EC) 37/2005 recording-instrument duty), c9 (records retained), c6 (transport-refrigeration dealers service vans annually); c8 risk if EN 12830 conformity is required.

title: Retrofit electronic brake performance monitoring (EBPMS) to cut laden roller-brake tests on older trailers
problem: DVSA's Guide to Maintaining Roadworthiness expects a brake efficiency test at every safety inspection (every ~6-13 weeks), ideally laden. Operators must load trailers or pay for test-centre or ATF slots, losing trailer days. Older trailers without OEM telematics can't use EBPMS, the accepted alternative. Brake defects remain a top DVSA prohibition and Traffic Commissioner issue.
who_suffers: Workshop teams arranging laden tests; transport managers facing DVSA/TC scrutiny
buyer: Fleet Engineering Manager / Transport Manager of a trailer fleet or trailer lessor
industry: UK semi-trailer fleets (general haulage, trailer rental and contract hire)
current_workaround: Roller brake tests at each PMI (often needing ballast or a laden trailer), decelerometer tests on the road, paid ATF/test-lane slots, OEM EBPMS only on new trailers.
sensor_concept: Trailer module: brake control-line pressure transducer, air-suspension pressure (load), IMU deceleration and GNSS speed, powered from the ISO 7638 supply, LTE-M; computes braking efficiency per braking event and produces a DVSA-style EBPMS report per PMI; alerts on degradation.
notes: Expect strong c4 (DVSA roadworthiness guide, O-licence undertakings, EBPMS recognition), c2/c3 (test every PMI with paid labour), c6 (trailer maintenance contractors and lessors), c9 (ongoing records); c8 risk on achieving accepted accuracy.

title: Trailer wheel-end fires from seized bearings or dragging brakes go unnoticed until the trailer is ablaze
problem: A dragging brake or failing hub bearing overheats over many miles and the driver can't feel it from the cab. A tyre or hub fire destroys trailer and load (~£30k-£100k) and closes motorway lanes. Lesser cases cause bearing collapse or wheel loss, with DVSA prohibitions and investigations.
who_suffers: Drivers; transport managers; fleet engineers
buyer: Fleet Engineering Manager at a trailer-operating haulier or trailer rental company
industry: UK semi-trailer fleets (general haulage, trailer rental and lessors)
current_workaround: Driver walkaround (informal hand-on-hub checks after long runs), PMI inspections every 6-10 weeks, infrared thermometer spot checks, tyre-service contractors' yard checks.
sensor_concept: Bolt-on hub-cap temperature sensors (BLE/sub-GHz) per wheel end feeding a trailer gateway on LTE-M powered from ISO 7638; alerts driver and office on abnormal rise or side-to-side delta; trend report to workshop for brake adjustment.
notes: Expect strong c1 (trailer and load fire value), c4 (O-licence maintenance obligations), c6 (tyre and maintenance contractors, trailer lessors), c8 (cheap temperature sensors); c2 risk if fires are rare per fleet.

title: Haulage depot oil separator overfills unnoticed and discharges diesel to surface-water drains
problem: Depots with refuelling points and wash bays rely on oil separators that should be inspected about every 6 months and emptied. When oil or silt exceeds capacity, oil passes into drains, leading to an Environment Agency pollution incident, prosecution and clean-up (~£10k-£100k+). Meanwhile the paid tanker emptying is booked by calendar rather than need.
who_suffers: Depot/yard managers; SHEQ managers
buyer: Depot Manager / SHEQ Manager of a haulage, bus or coach operator
industry: HGV, bus and coach depots with diesel refuelling and vehicle wash bays
current_workaround: Fixed-interval (~6-monthly) inspection and emptying by waste-tanker contractors, mains-wired oil alarms on some Class 1 separators (often disconnected), visual dips.
sensor_concept: Battery probe kit in the separator chamber: oil-layer probe (capacitive/conductivity) plus ultrasonic liquid/silt level; NB-IoT/LoRaWAN; alerts on oil depth and high level; empty-on-demand report for the contractor and an evidence log for the EA.
notes: Expect strong c4 (EA pollution offences, BS EN 858-2 inspection and alarm guidance, GPP), c3 (paid 6-monthly visits), c6 (interceptor service and waste-tanker contractors already visit), c1 (EA fines); c8 risk on oil-probe cost.

title: Reefer-unit diesel tank, invisible to truck telematics, runs dry or is siphoned and the chilled load is lost
problem: Trailer refrigeration units run from their own ~200-250 L diesel tank, which the truck's CAN telematics can't see. Drivers forget to fill it, or thieves drain it at truck stops; the unit stops and a chilled or frozen load (~£10k-£60k) is rejected at the supermarket RDC.
who_suffers: Drivers; transport planners; customers rejecting loads
buyer: Transport Manager of a temperature-controlled haulier or own-account food distributor
industry: Temperature-controlled trailer fleets serving supermarket RDCs, especially SMEs with older TRUs lacking OEM telematics
current_workaround: Driver dips or reads the gauge before departure, TRU alarm codes visible only at the unit, OEM telematics on newer units only, 'deterioration' cover claims with excesses.
sensor_concept: Retrofit ultrasonic or capacitive fuel-level sensor in the TRU tank, return-air temperature probe and unit-running detection (vibration/current); LTE-M on trailer power with battery backup; alerts on theft-like drops, low fuel versus remaining journey, or unit stopped; pre-trip fuel report.
notes: Expect strong c1 (load value), c2 (run-outs and thefts recur), c6 (TRU service dealers); c7 gap in older/mixed TRU fleets without OEM telematics.

title: Load-securing straps slacken in transit on steel, timber and machinery loads, triggering DVSA load-security prohibitions
problem: Ratchet straps relax as loads settle. DVSA roadside checks issue immediate prohibitions for insecure loads: the driver is stopped until re-secured, OCRS points accrue and Traffic Commissioner action becomes possible. Shifted loads also damage goods and vehicles (~£2k-£20k) or spill on the carriageway.
who_suffers: Flatbed drivers re-checking straps at every stop; transport managers
buyer: Transport Manager of a flatbed steel, timber or plant haulage operator
industry: Flatbed and curtainsider hauliers carrying steel coils and sections, timber and machinery
current_workaround: Drivers re-check and re-tension straps at stops (as DVSA guidance advises), load-security training, edge protectors and anti-slip mats; nothing during driving.
sensor_concept: Inline strap-tension link sensors (strain gauge) with BLE to an in-cab LTE-M gateway or driver phone; alerts when tension drops by a set percentage; per-journey log proving the load was secured, for DVSA and claims.
notes: Expect strong c4 (DVSA load-security guidance and prohibitions, Road Traffic Act s40A), c2 (every load), c10 (DVSA enforcement data plus trade press); c8 risk on per-strap BOM, c7 risk from existing strap-sensor products.

title: Broiler live-haul lorries in summer heat: dead-on-arrival birds spike with no in-load temperature data
problem: Heat and humidity build up inside poultry modules during loading delays and traffic. The processing plant's Official Veterinarian records dead-on-arrival (DOA) birds for every delivery. A bad load can lose ~1-2% of ~6,000 birds (~£2k-£5k) and trigger welfare investigations under WATO, and long-journey vehicles legally need temperature monitoring.
who_suffers: Catching crews, drivers, live-haul managers, growers paid on birds delivered
buyer: Live-Haul / Agricultural Transport Manager at a poultry integrator
industry: UK broiler and turkey live-haul fleets (integrator-owned or contracted)
current_workaround: Driver judgment, weather-based reductions in loading density, curtain and fan adjustments, occasional trial dataloggers, DOA spreadsheets after the fact.
sensor_concept: Multi-point temperature and humidity sensors in module stacks with an LTE-M gateway on the lorry; real-time heat-index alert to driver and plant lairage; per-load welfare record correlated with DOA.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Welfare of Animals (Transport) Order 2006 / Reg (EC) 1/2005), c2 (daily loads), c1 (DOA losses per load), c5 (integrator live-haul manager).

title: Burst hydraulic hose on skip loaders, hook-loaders and RCVs sprays oil along the road before the driver notices
problem: A hose or seal failure empties the hydraulic tank over miles of road. The highway authority or National Highways contractors close lanes and recharge the clean-up (~£5k-£50k), and insurers may dispute cover for poor maintenance. If the pump runs dry it is destroyed (~£2k-£5k).
who_suffers: Drivers; fleet engineers; insurers
buyer: Fleet Engineer / Workshop Manager of a skip-hire, waste or tipper fleet
industry: Skip-loader, hook-loader, refuse-collection and grab/tipper fleets with PTO hydraulics
current_workaround: Daily walkaround check of hoses and oil level, mobile hose-repair callouts, reactive spill kits, PMI inspections.
sensor_concept: Hydraulic reservoir level sensor (float/ultrasonic), oil temperature and GNSS on LTE-M powered from the vehicle; in-cab buzzer plus office alert on a rapid level drop; spill-trail location for responders; hose service log.
notes: Expect strong c1 (recharged clean-up plus pump damage), c6 (mobile hose-repair networks and body builders already serve these fleets), c8 (simple level sensing); c2 frequency per fleet needs evidence.

title: Farm user-worked level crossing gates left open let livestock onto the line
problem: On private user-worked crossings, the authorised user must shut the gates. Gates left open let cattle and sheep onto the railway, causing train strikes, line blocks and delay compensation (~£ thousands per incident) plus livestock losses. Network Rail level crossing managers already make cyclical inspection visits to every crossing.
who_suffers: Signallers, train drivers, Network Rail level crossing managers, farmers
buyer: Network Rail Route Level Crossing Manager (or Route Asset Manager, Level Crossings)
industry: GB rail user-worked crossings on farm accommodation and private roads
current_workaround: Signage, crossing telephones, periodic inspections and risk assessments (ALCRM), letters to authorised users, closure programmes, costly miniature stop lights at high-risk sites.
sensor_concept: Battery magnetic/tilt gate-position sensor on each gate leaf, LoRaWAN/NB-IoT; alert to route control and the authorised user's phone if a gate stays open beyond N minutes; usage counts feed the crossing risk assessment.
notes: Expect strong c4 (ORR/NR level crossing risk duties, statutory user duty to close gates), c2 (daily gate use), c3 (inspection visits), c10 (RAIB reports); c5 risk from Network Rail procurement.

title: Silted track-drainage catchpits and culverts overflow in storms, flooding cuttings and forcing speed restrictions
problem: Silted catchpits and culverts on earthworks overflow in heavy rain, saturating the trackbed or washing out embankments; Carmont 2020 is the extreme case. Routine failures bring emergency speed restrictions, delay compensation and emergency jetting (~£5k-£50k per event).
who_suffers: Network Rail drainage engineers, track maintenance teams, operators and passengers
buyer: Network Rail Route Drainage Engineer / Asset Engineer (Drainage)
industry: GB mainline track drainage, catchpits and culverts at high-risk earthworks
current_workaround: Cyclical drainage inspections and CCTV surveys, extreme-weather cess walks and watchmen at known sites, reactive jetting by drainage contractors.
sensor_concept: Ultrasonic or pressure water-level sensor in the catchpit or culvert inlet on battery LoRaWAN/NB-IoT; alerts when level exceeds outfall capacity during rain; data prioritises jetting by framework contractors.
notes: Expect strong c1 (delay and emergency works), c4 (NR drainage standards, RAIB Carmont recommendations), c6 (drainage framework contractors on site); c5/c7 risk from NR procurement and existing remote-condition-monitoring vendors.

title: Repeatedly struck low rail bridges: every strike halts trains until a bridge examiner attends
problem: GB rail bridges are struck ~1,600-2,000 times a year (Network Rail cites ~£13k average cost per strike), and some bridges are hit ~20-30 times a year. Trains are stopped or cautioned until an examiner checks the structure, so delay compensation accrues even when there is no damage.
who_suffers: Signallers, on-call bridge examiners, passengers; hauliers facing Traffic Commissioner action
buyer: Network Rail Route Asset Manager (Structures)
industry: GB rail over-road bridges with low headroom
current_workaround: Signage and awareness campaigns, height-warning systems at a few sites, on-call examiners attending each strike, CCTV at some bridges.
sensor_concept: Accelerometer and tilt sensor on the bridge deck and parapet on LTE-M; classifies impact energy and permanent displacement within seconds so signallers can resume at caution sooner; strike log supports cost recovery from hauliers.
notes: Expect strong c1 (NR per-strike cost), c2 (most-bashed bridges struck roughly every 1-3 weeks), c10 (NR data, trade press, Traffic Commissioner actions); c5/c6 risk from NR procurement.

title: Unstaffed station platforms and footbridges ice over before gritting is triggered, leading to slip claims
problem: Many small stations are unstaffed, so gritting runs on forecasts or rounds. Localised ice causes passenger slips and falls, with public liability claims (~£5k-£50k each), while mobile teams spend winter nights on gritting rounds.
who_suffers: Passengers, mobile station teams, TOC claims teams
buyer: TOC Head of Stations / Station Facilities Manager
industry: GB train operating companies' unstaffed and small stations and footbridges
current_workaround: Forecast-triggered gritting rounds by mobile staff or contractors, salt bins, station inspection checklists, reactive response to reports.
sensor_concept: Surface temperature (IR/contact) with air temperature and humidity on platform and footbridge, LoRaWAN/LTE-M; per-station ice prediction dispatches gritting; time-stamped condition and gritting evidence for claims defence.
notes: Expect strong c1 (slip claim costs), c2 (frost days every winter), c3 (gritting rounds); c4 via Occupiers' Liability; c7 gap: road weather stations are expensive for small stations.

title: Shore-supply trips at stabling sidings overnight leave trains with flat batteries and cold cabs, causing morning cancellations
problem: Units stabled overnight sit on shore power. If the supply trips or a plug is knocked out, batteries drain and heating fails, so the unit can't be prepared in the morning. The result is cancellations and delay-attribution penalties (~£ thousands per incident).
who_suffers: Depot shunters and prep staff, fleet controllers, passengers
buyer: TOC Fleet Engineering Manager / Depot Manager (or train maintainer's depot manager)
industry: GB EMU/DMU stabling sidings and depots
current_workaround: Night-shift walk-rounds checking shore connections, prep teams arriving early, fault reports after failures.
sensor_concept: Clamp-on current transformers on each shore-supply outlet plus supply voltage, LoRaWAN gateway with cellular backhaul; alerts the controller when an outlet stops drawing current; nightly 'all units charging' report. Fixed infrastructure, so no rolling-stock certification is needed.
notes: Expect strong c2 (nightly), c3 (night walk-rounds), c1 (cancellation and delay costs), c8 (off-the-shelf CTs); c5 buyer is TOC fleet engineering.

title: Lift pits flood at open-air station footbridge lifts, taking step-free access out of service for days
problem: Rain and groundwater enter the pits of outdoor station lifts. Water damages buffers and controls, and the lift is out of service until it is pumped out and repaired (~£2k-£10k per event), stranding wheelchair users and drawing ORR and accessibility scrutiny.
who_suffers: Disabled passengers, station staff, lift maintainers
buyer: Network Rail/TOC Station Asset Manager (MEP) / Lift and Escalator Engineer
industry: GB station lifts (Access for All footbridges), bus and tram interchange lifts
current_workaround: Monthly maintenance visits by the lift contractor, sump pumps that often fail silently, reactive callouts after passenger complaints.
sensor_concept: Water-presence and level sensor in the lift pit plus sump-pump run-current monitor, battery LoRaWAN/LTE-M; alerts the maintainer before water reaches equipment; availability log.
notes: Expect strong c2 (rain-driven recurrence), c6 (lift contractors visit monthly), c1 (repair and outage costs), c4 (LOLER and accessibility obligations); c7: OEM lift telemetry may not cover pits.

title: Signalling equipment buildings overheat when air-conditioning fails in heatwaves, causing signal failures
problem: Lineside relocatable equipment buildings (REBs) house signalling electronics cooled by AC. A failed unit in summer pushes temperatures past equipment limits, causing signal or axle-counter failures, delay minutes and emergency call-outs (~£10k+ per incident).
who_suffers: Signalling maintenance teams, operators, passengers
buyer: Network Rail Route Signal Maintenance Engineer / Signalling Asset Engineer
industry: GB rail lineside signalling equipment buildings
current_workaround: Planned HVAC maintenance visits, partial remote condition monitoring, reactive response after failures, temporary cooling in heatwaves.
sensor_concept: Battery temperature/humidity sensor, AC compressor current clamp and door sensor on LoRaWAN/LTE-M; alerts when internal temperature rises or AC stops cycling; heatwave dashboard to prioritise visits.
notes: Expect strong c1 (delay costs), c2 (summer recurrence), c6 (HVAC contractors visit REBs); c5/c7 risk from NR procurement and existing RCM.

title: Blanket heat speed restrictions on welded rail because rail temperature is measured at too few points
problem: When forecast rail temperatures pass critical thresholds, Network Rail imposes blanket speed restrictions over wide areas. Each hot day costs delay compensation; denser local rail-temperature data would allow targeted restrictions and focused patrols.
who_suffers: Track engineers, operators, passengers
buyer: Network Rail Route Track Engineer / Weather Resilience lead
industry: GB continuous welded rail (also heritage lines)
current_workaround: A limited number of rail temperature probes, forecasts, hot-weather watchmen and patrols at known sites, blanket emergency speed restrictions.
sensor_concept: Magnet-mounted rail-web temperature sensor on battery LoRaWAN/NB-IoT, densely deployed at suspect-stress sites; threshold alerts and patrol prioritisation.
notes: Expect strong c1 (delay costs), c2 (repeated hot days each summer), c3 (patrols/watchmen); c5/c7 risk from NR procurement and existing probe vendors.

title: LPG cylinder cages at retail stockists are raided for scrap and run empty between delivery runs
problem: Calor has reported ~200,000 cylinders stolen in a year (~£9m). Garages, garden centres and farm shops holding cylinder cages lose cylinders overnight, empty cages mean lost sales, and distributor drivers count cages by hand on each restock visit.
who_suffers: Stockist staff, distributor delivery drivers, distributor retail managers
buyer: Regional Dealer/Retail Network Manager at an LPG cylinder distributor (or independent LPG dealer owner)
industry: UK LPG cylinder retail stockist network (garages, garden centres, builders merchants, farm shops)
current_workaround: Locked cages, manual stock counts by drivers on each delivery, fixed delivery schedules, police reports and scrapyard warnings.
sensor_concept: Cage-mounted battery module: door reed switch, tamper accelerometer and ToF or weight-bar estimate of full cylinders; LTE-M/NB-IoT; after-hours intrusion alerts; stock levels drive restock route planning.
notes: Expect strong c1 (theft value cited by Calor), c2 (daily sales, weekly restock), c3 (manual counting), c6 (distributor owns the cages and visits weekly); c7 gap: no cage-specific product.

title: Metered LPG estates and park-home sites: manual meter reads, estimated bills and undetected underground leaks
problem: On LPG metered estates, the supplier runs a central tank and bills each home from its meter. Reads are manual or estimated, which causes bill disputes. Leaks in underground pipework only show up when tank deliveries fail to reconcile with meter totals (lost gas ~£ thousands/yr per estate), and HSE research flags the leak risk to park homes.
who_suffers: Residents with shock bills; supplier billing teams; park owners
buyer: Metered Estates Manager at an LPG supplier (or park-home site owner reselling gas)
industry: LPG metered estates (new-build housing, residential park-home and holiday parks)
current_workaround: Meter-reader site visits, customer self-reads, estimated billing, leak surveys and pressure tests after reconciliation gaps.
sensor_concept: Non-intrusive pulse/magnetometer reader clipped to existing diaphragm gas meters (no gas contact), LoRaWAN gateway per estate; daily automatic reads; tank telemetry versus sum-of-meters reconciliation flags leaks; night-flow anomaly alerts.
notes: Expect strong c2/c3 (regular meter-reading visits), c6 (supplier owns site and network), c8 (cheap reader, no gas contact), c4 (gas resale/billing rules, HSE leak research); c7 risk from AMR incumbents.

title: Commercial heating-oil tanks leak slowly into bunds or the ground, and 'gradual pollution' exclusions leave owners paying the clean-up
problem: Oil storage regulations require bunding for commercial tanks over 200 L, but bunds fill with rainwater or oil unnoticed and single-skin tanks seep. Many policies exclude gradual pollution, so the clean-up (~£10k-£100k) and Environment Agency action fall on the business.
who_suffers: Farm, school, church and small-business owners; facilities managers
buyer: Facilities Manager / Estate Manager (schools, care homes, rural businesses)
industry: Commercial and institutional heating-oil storage off the gas grid
current_workaround: Annual OFTEC tank inspection, visual bund checks, manual pumping of rainwater, occasional wired bund alarms, reconciling oil use against deliveries.
sensor_concept: Battery bund sensor that distinguishes oil from water (conductivity/optical) plus tank level-drop analysis, NB-IoT/LTE-M; alerts on oil in the bund or unexplained level loss; annual compliance pack for insurer and EA.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Control of Pollution (Oil Storage) (England) Regs 2001), c1 (clean-up costs, uninsured exclusions), c6 (oil distributors and OFTEC technicians visit); c7 risk from existing bund alarms.

title: Forklift LPG cylinders run out at warehouses because cage stock isn't visible to the gas supplier
problem: Sites running LPG counterbalance forklifts keep cylinder cages refilled by a weekly delivery. Demand peaks or missed deliveries leave trucks idle (lost shift output ~£ thousands) or force emergency deliveries (~£100-£300 surcharge), and full/empty counts are done by hand.
who_suffers: Forklift drivers, warehouse shift managers
buyer: Warehouse Operations Manager / Site Facilities Manager
industry: Warehouses, manufacturers and builders merchants using LPG forklifts
current_workaround: Manual cage counts and phone orders, standing weekly deliveries, oversized cylinder stocks, distributor driver counts on each drop.
sensor_concept: Cage load-cell bars or ToF count of full versus empty cylinders plus door sensor, LTE-M; distributor portal auto-schedules deliveries; usage-per-shift report; alert on unauthorised access.
notes: Expect strong c2 (weekly deliveries), c3 (manual counting and ordering), c6 (gas distributor owns cylinders and visits weekly); c1 downtime cost needs sourcing.

title: Wood-pellet stores for commercial biomass boilers run empty unnoticed, leaving schools and care homes without heat
problem: Pellet silos and bunkers have no reliable level reading. When pellets run out, the boiler locks out, the building goes cold, and the site pays an emergency delivery premium plus a restart callout (~£500-£2k); care homes face welfare issues. Deliveries need ~3-7 days' notice.
who_suffers: Site caretakers, residents and pupils, biomass maintenance contractors
buyer: Estates/Facilities Manager (schools, care homes, rural estates, holiday parks)
industry: Commercial wood-pellet biomass boilers (~50-500 kW)
current_workaround: Caretaker opens the hatch and looks weekly, fixed delivery schedules, boiler low-pellet alarms only at the hopper (too late).
sensor_concept: Dust-tolerant ToF/ultrasonic level sensor at the silo top plus boiler status contact, LTE-M; days-to-empty forecast pushed to the pellet supplier; low-level alerts.
notes: Expect strong c2 (weekly checks), c3 (caretaker checks, emergency delivery fees), c6 (pellet suppliers and biomass service contractors visit); c4 weak; c8 dust risk.

title: Off-grid pubs and cafés on 47 kg propane cylinder banks run out at weekends because nobody sees the changeover flip to reserve
problem: Auto-changeover valves switch to the reserve bank silently, and the reserve empties before anyone reorders. The kitchen or heating goes down on a busy weekend (lost trade ~£1k-£5k per day), and out-of-hours deliveries cost a premium.
who_suffers: Chefs, licensees, café owners
buyer: Owner/Licensee of an off-grid hospitality business; or an LPG dealer offering managed supply
industry: Off-gas-grid pubs, cafés, B&Bs and campsites using 47 kg propane cylinder banks
current_workaround: Visual check of the changeover indicator, staff told to phone the dealer, standing orders, carrying spare cylinders.
sensor_concept: Clip-on sensor reading the changeover valve flag (magnetic/optical) or a load-cell platform under the cylinders, LTE-M; alerts dealer and owner when the valve switches to reserve; auto-reorder.
notes: Expect strong c2 (frequent changeovers), c6 (dealer delivers and could bundle), c8 (cheap); c4 weak; c7 risk from consumer ultrasonic cylinder gauges.

title: Water and diesel bug build up in standby generator fuel tanks, so the generator fails during a power cut
problem: Standby generators at care homes, hospitals, telecom sites and farms sit idle. Condensation water and microbial growth block filters, so the set fails under load in an outage (loss ~£5k-£50k+). Fuel testing and polishing contractors sample about once a year.
who_suffers: Facilities managers, residents/patients, operations teams
buyer: Facilities/Estates Manager responsible for standby power
industry: Standby diesel generator fuel tanks (care homes, hospitals, water and telecom sites, farms)
current_workaround: Annual fuel sampling and lab test, periodic polishing by contractor, monthly generator test runs, manual water-finding paste dips.
sensor_concept: Tank-bottom free-water probe (capacitive/conductivity), fuel level and temperature on NB-IoT/LTE-M; alerts when water appears or rises; condition-based polishing schedule; records for resilience audits.
notes: Expect strong c3 (paid testing and polishing), c6 (fuel suppliers, polishing contractors and generator engineers visit), c4 (NHS HTM 06-01 and resilience audits); c2 risk (failure rare).

title: Remote-fill oil tanks overfill during delivery because the driver can't see the tank, and the distributor pays for the spill
problem: Where the fill point is remote from the tank, BS 5410/OFTEC call for overfill prevention or an alarm. Failed or missing devices mean spills during delivery, with clean-up (~£5k-£50k) disputed between distributor and customer, plus Environment Agency pollution liability.
who_suffers: Tanker drivers, distributor operations and insurers, customers
buyer: Operations Director of a heating-oil distributor (or the distributor's insurer)
industry: Heating-oil distribution to commercial and farm tanks with remote fill points
current_workaround: Drivers estimate ullage from the customer's gauge or history, mechanical overfill valves and whistles, delivering a set volume rather than 'fill', post-spill blame disputes.
sensor_concept: Tank high-level/ullage sensor streaming live to the driver's handheld during delivery (BLE plus LTE-M), auto-logging pre- and post-delivery levels as evidence; also supports delivery scheduling.
notes: Expect strong c4 (BS 5410/OFTEC overfill requirements, Oil Storage Regs), c6 (distributor delivers and could own the device), c1 (spill costs); c7 risk from tank-gauge incumbents.

title: Church roof alarms rely on phone-line diallers the PSTN switch-off breaks, putting lead-theft cover at risk
problem: The main church insurer limits metal-theft cover unless an approved, monitored roof alarm is fitted. Existing alarms cost ~£3k-£5k plus maintenance, and many use landline diallers that fail with the digital switchover. A lead theft costs from ~£10k to ~£400k per church.
who_suffers: Churchwardens, PCCs, diocesan advisers
buyer: Churchwarden / PCC (with Diocesan Advisory Committee approval), reached via insurer-approved installers
industry: Church of England and other historic places of worship with lead or copper roofs
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Approved roof alarms with monitored diallers, SmartWater marking, replacing lead with substitute materials, volunteer vigilance, faculty (List B) permission for alarms.
sensor_concept: Battery wireless roof sensors (PIR plus vibration on lead sheets) with an LTE-M/LoRaWAN cellular communicator (no phone line or mains); monitored alert routing to an ARC and keyholders; insurer compliance status reports.
notes: Expect strong c4 (insurer electronic protection condition), c1 (lead theft costs), c6 (insurer-approved installers and diocesan channels); c2 risk (theft rare per church, though alarm tests are monthly).

title: Sunday-only heating dries out historic pipe organs, cracking soundboards and leatherwork
problem: Rapid warm-up for services drops relative humidity sharply, and repeated cycles crack wooden soundboards and leather, causing ciphers and costly repairs (a reservoir ~£2.5k; restorations from tens of thousands to £100k+). Diocesan guidance limits heating ramp rates, but almost nobody measures them.
who_suffers: Organists, PCCs, organ builders
buyer: PCC Treasurer / Churchwarden (fabric) on the organ adviser's recommendation; cathedral Clerk of Works
industry: Churches and cathedrals with historic pipe organs
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Organ tuner visits 1-4 times a year, dial hygrometers, diocesan organ adviser guidance, humidifiers in the organ case, background heating.
sensor_concept: RH/temperature logger in the organ case plus church air, LoRaWAN/LTE-M; alerts on rapid RH drop or excessive heating ramp; advice for the heating controller; report shared with the organ builder before tuning visits.
notes: Expect strong c6 (organ builders and tuners visit regularly; diocesan organ advisers), c2 (weekly heating cycles); c1 repair costs need sourcing; c4 moderate (DAC/faculty guidance).

title: Village and church halls left empty for weeks freeze and flood, breaching insurers' unoccupancy conditions
problem: Halls used intermittently, with heating off and water on over holidays or closures, get burst pipes and escape-of-water damage (~£10k-£50k). The claim may be cut if unoccupancy conditions (drain down, maintain heat, inspect weekly) weren't met.
who_suffers: Volunteer hall committees and trustees, user groups
buyer: Hall Management Committee Chair/Treasurer (charity trustees)
industry: Village halls, church halls, scout and guide huts run by charities
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Volunteer weekly inspections when unoccupied, boiler frost settings, draining down, insurer guidance via ACRE and rural community councils.
sensor_concept: Battery temperature sensor plus leak/flow sensor on the rising main (optional auto shut-off valve), LTE-M; frost and leak alerts to several trustees; automatic weekly inspection log for the insurer.
notes: Expect strong c4 (insurer unoccupancy conditions), c3 (weekly volunteer inspections), c6 (ACRE network and specialist hall insurers); c7 risk from generic leak sensors.

title: Mosques and church halls with intermittent use can't evidence the weekly flushing and monthly sentinel temperatures that Legionella control requires
problem: HSE ACOP L8/HSG274 require a Legionella risk assessment, weekly flushing of little-used outlets and monthly hot/cold sentinel temperature checks. Wudu/ablution areas and halls with sporadic use stagnate. Water-hygiene contractors charge per monthly visit, and outbreaks bring HSE enforcement.
who_suffers: Trustees and facility volunteers, worshippers, cleaners
buyer: Mosque Trustee / Facilities Manager; Diocesan Property or Facilities Officer
industry: Mosques with ablution facilities, gurdwaras, church and community halls with showers
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Paid monthly contractor temperature checks, volunteer flushing logs on paper, annual risk assessment.
sensor_concept: Clamp-on pipe temperature sensors on sentinel outlets with use detection from the temperature signature, LoRaWAN/LTE-M; auto-logs flushing and temperatures; alerts when an outlet is unused for more than 7 days or out of range; L8 compliance report.
notes: Expect strong c4 (ACOP L8 and HSG274 with HSE enforcement), c2 (weekly/monthly tasks), c3 (contractor visit fees), c6 (water-hygiene contractors), c9 (records).

title: Charity clothing banks are emptied by thieves or overflow into fly-tipping before the collection van arrives
problem: Organised theft from textile banks and bank removals cost charities heavily (estimates of ~£15m/yr sector-wide; one charity ~£850k/yr; replacing a bank up to ~£1.5k). Full banks attract side-waste and complaints from landowners and councils, while collection rounds run on fixed schedules.
who_suffers: Charity collection managers, host sites (supermarkets, schools), councils
buyer: Head of Donated Goods / Textile Collections at a charity trading company
industry: Charity and commercial textile/clothing bank networks
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Fixed-route collections, anti-theft chutes, CCTV at some sites, staff reporting overflows, police reports.
sensor_concept: Ultrasonic fill sensor, door/chute tamper accelerometer and GNSS (to detect bank removal) on battery LTE-M/NB-IoT; route optimisation plus theft alerts with evidence.
notes: Expect strong c1 (sourced theft losses), c2 (weekly collections), c3 (collection rounds), c10 (letsrecycle trade press plus news); c7 risk from waste fill-sensor incumbents.

title: Community defibrillator guardians walk to cabinets weekly; failed heaters and unreturned AEDs still go unnoticed
problem: Guardians must check the AED and its outdoor cabinet weekly and log readiness on The Circuit. A failed cabinet heater lets pads and battery freeze, AEDs aren't returned after use, and cabinets get vandalised (cabinet ~£500-£700, AED ~£900-£1,200). An unready AED is often discovered only in an emergency.
who_suffers: Volunteer guardians, parish and town councils, church and hall committees
buyer: Parish/Town Council Clerk or hall/church trustee, reached via the AED supplier or the charity that installs cabinets
industry: Community public-access defibrillators at churches, village halls and parish councils
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Weekly guardian walk-and-check, paper or Circuit log, ambulance service notifications after use.
sensor_concept: Cabinet module: door switch, temperature and an optical sensor reading the AED status indicator, battery LTE-M; auto-updates readiness; alerts on door opening (AED use), cold cabinet or status-light fault.
notes: Expect strong c2 (weekly checks), c3 (guardian labour), c6 (AED and cabinet suppliers, ambulance trusts); c1 weak (replacement under £2k) unless liability is evidenced.

title: Blocked valley gutters and hopper heads on church roofs overflow unseen, soaking walls and causing rot
problem: Water ingress from blocked gutters and downpipes is the biggest driver of decay in churches. It is spotted only at quinquennial inspections or when damp appears, and repairs run ~£5k-£50k. Maintenance schemes recommend twice-yearly gutter clearance by contractors.
who_suffers: Churchwardens, PCCs, inspecting architects
buyer: Churchwarden / PCC Fabric Officer; Diocesan or Cathedral Property Manager
industry: Historic churches and listed places of worship
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Twice-yearly gutter clearance through maintenance services, volunteer checks in rain, quinquennial inspection reports.
sensor_concept: Float or water-level sensor in the valley gutter or hopper head plus rain gauge, battery LoRaWAN/LTE-M; alerts when water stays high after rain (a blockage); evidence log for the maintenance contractor and quinquennial architect.
notes: Expect strong c2 (monthly rain events), c3 (paid clearance visits), c4 (quinquennial inspection duty under church measures), c6 (church maintenance contractors and schemes).

title: Open-church volunteer keyholders forget to lock up at dusk, breaching insurer security conditions and inviting theft
problem: Churches kept open by day rely on volunteer rotas to unlock and lock. A missed lock-up leaves the building open overnight to theft of silver, vandalism or arson, and a claim may be reduced if security conditions were breached (losses ~£2k-£20k+).
who_suffers: Keyholder volunteers, churchwardens
buyer: Churchwarden / PCC Secretary; Churches Conservation Trust regional manager
industry: Open churches (CofE parishes, Churches Conservation Trust and similar trusts)
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Volunteer rotas, WhatsApp reminders, timer locks on some doors, insurer guidance on open churches.
sensor_concept: Door and lock-state sensor (magnetic plus bolt position) on main doors, battery LTE-M; alerts the rota if not locked by sunset plus X minutes; daily open/close log; optional after-hours PIR.
notes: Expect strong c2 (daily), c3 (rota labour), c4 (insurer conditions for open churches); c1 risk (moderate loss per incident).

title: Parish register cabinets must hold set temperature and humidity, with readings recorded and kept for 12 months, but readings are rarely taken
problem: The Parochial Registers and Records Measure 1978 (Sch. 2) requires registers kept in church to sit in a vented steel cabinet with a thermometer and hygrometer, with readings recorded, kept for at least 12 months and made available for inspection. Damp vestries cause mould and paper damage, and failed inspections push deposit to the record office.
who_suffers: Incumbents, churchwardens, diocesan inspectors of records
buyer: Incumbent / PCC (churchwardens), on the diocesan registrar's or archivist's recommendation
industry: Church of England parishes keeping registers in church
sector: Places of worship, community halls & charities
current_workaround: Dial thermometer and hygrometer in the cabinet, sporadic handwritten readings, depositing registers with the county record office.
sensor_concept: Small temperature/RH logger inside the register cabinet on LoRaWAN/LTE-M (or BLE to a church gateway); automatic statutory record; out-of-range alerts; exportable log for the inspector.
notes: Expect strong c4 (named statutory record-keeping duty), c9 (12-month retention), c2 (continuous duty); c1 weak (losses hard to price), so best bundled with other church sensors.

title: Floor-stored grain heats in hot spots between weekly spear probes; loads rejected for insects or mycotoxins
problem: Red Tractor assessors expect records of crop temperature and moisture monitoring in store (weekly after harvest). Manual probing misses hot spots, and heating grain leads to insect infestation, downgrades or rejection (~£2k-£10k per load or heap) and claims from merchants.
who_suffers: Farm managers and grain-store staff
buyer: Farm Manager / Arable Business Owner; on-farm co-op store manager
industry: UK on-farm floor-store and bin grain storage (wheat, barley, oilseed rape)
current_workaround: Weekly spear-probe temperature readings on paper, aeration fans on thermostats, a calibrated probe shown at audit, merchant sampling at collection.
sensor_concept: Wireless grain temperature (plus RH) spears left in the heap on battery LoRaWAN/LTE-M; hot-spot alerts; aeration fan advice; automatic Red Tractor-ready monitoring record.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Red Tractor storage monitoring records), c2 (weekly), c3 (manual probing), c6 (merchants and agronomists visit); c7 risk from existing wireless spear products, so the gap needs evidence.

title: Processing-potato box stores drift below set temperature, causing sugar build-up and fry-colour rejections by processors
problem: Processing potatoes are held at ~8-10°C. Cold spots or CO2 build-up in box stores cause sweetening and dark fry colour, so crisp and chip processors downgrade or reject loads (~£5k-£30k per batch) under contract specifications. Store managers walk the stores daily.
who_suffers: Store managers, contract growers
buyer: Farm/Store Manager of a contract potato grower; processor's Raw Material/Agronomy Manager
industry: UK processing-potato storage (crisp and chip contracts)
current_workaround: Daily store walks with a hand thermometer, a central controller with few sensors, fry tests by processor field staff, CO2 venting.
sensor_concept: Box-level wireless temperature, CO2 and RH sensors spread through the store on LoRaWAN; maps cold spots and CO2; alerts; data shared with the processor's raw-material team.
notes: Expect strong c1 (contract rejection costs), c2 (daily store walks), c6 (processor field technicians and store engineering firms visit), c4 (contract specs and assurance).

title: Small nurseries lose whole glasshouse crops when gas or paraffin heaters fail on a frosty night
problem: A heater or boiler lockout or a power cut on a frost night kills bedding, young plants or overwintered stock (~£10k-£100k of crop). Small growers lack climate computers, and glasshouse crop insurance may require a low-temperature alarm.
who_suffers: Grower-owners getting up at night to check heaters
buyer: Nursery Owner / Production Manager
industry: Small and medium ornamental nurseries, garden-centre growing units, heated polytunnels
current_workaround: Late-night and early-morning checks, max-min thermometers, landline dialler frost alarms, backup heaters.
sensor_concept: Air temperature sensors plus heater or boiler status (flue temperature or current), LTE-M; escalating call/SMS to several staff; frost-night log for the insurer.
notes: Expect strong c1 (crop value), c2 (cold nights every winter), c3 (night checks), c6 (heating engineers and horticultural suppliers); c4 if an insurer condition is evidenced.

title: Table-top strawberry fertigation fails on a hot day and substrate dries out within hours
problem: Substrate-grown soft fruit depends on fertigation pumps and valves. A blocked filter, failed valve or pump trip on a hot day stresses plants and cuts yield (~£5k-£20k per tunnel block), so growers walk the lines checking drippers.
who_suffers: Growers, irrigation managers
buyer: Head Grower / Irrigation Manager at a soft-fruit farm
industry: UK table-top/substrate strawberry and raspberry production under polytunnels
current_workaround: Daily walking checks, drain-percentage measured by hand, controller alarms only at the head unit, moisture sensors in a few bags.
sensor_concept: Line-end pressure sensors plus a drain-cup volume/EC sensor per block on LoRaWAN; alerts on pressure loss or no drainage; daily irrigation record.
notes: Expect strong c2 (daily irrigation), c3 (labour walks), c1 (crop value per block), c6 (fertigation installers and agronomists); c7 risk from substrate-sensor vendors.

title: Abstraction licences require metered records and hands-off-flow stops, but meters are read by hand and breaches are prosecuted
problem: Abstraction licences require metering, records and returns, and some require abstraction to stop when river flow falls below a threshold. Over-abstraction and false returns are prosecuted (~£4k-£8k penalties in recent cases), and licences can be curtailed in drought.
who_suffers: Irrigating farmers and farm managers
buyer: Farm Manager / Irrigation Manager (the licence holder)
industry: UK spray-irrigated potatoes and vegetables on surface or groundwater abstraction licences
current_workaround: Manual meter readings (daily or weekly in season), spreadsheets, annual returns, EA notices of flow restrictions, meter calibration visits.
sensor_concept: Pulse/magnetic reader on the abstraction meter plus optional river-level feed, LTE-M/LoRaWAN; automatic volume log against daily and annual licence limits; alerts before caps; return-ready report.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Water Resources Act licence conditions plus EA prosecutions), c2 (frequent readings in season), c3 (manual reading), c9 (records), c6 (irrigation dealers).

title: Hose-reel irrigators stop overnight (pump trip, burst pipe, jammed reel) and staff drive the fields at 2 am to check
problem: Rain-guns run unattended at night. A stoppage wastes the irrigation window (quality loss on potatoes and vegetables ~£ thousands) or floods a headland, so staff do night checks and licensed water is wasted.
who_suffers: Irrigation staff on night rounds
buyer: Farm Manager / Irrigation Manager
industry: UK hose-reel/rain-gun irrigation of potatoes, vegetables and salads
current_workaround: Night drives to check reels, reel shut-off switches, SMS reel computers on newer reels only.
sensor_concept: Retrofit reel module: inlet pressure sensor, reel rotation (magnet/IMU) and GNSS, LTE-M; alerts on pressure loss or a stalled reel; run log.
notes: Expect strong c2 (daily in season), c3 (night labour), c6 (irrigation dealers service reels); c7 risk from OEM reel telemetry.

title: Thieves strip GPS receivers and screens from tractors overnight, halting drilling and spraying
problem: Theft of GPS receivers and displays from farm machinery is a well-publicised rural crime. Each kit costs ~£10k-£20k, the farm loses work days at drilling, and insurers push security measures while premiums rise after claims.
who_suffers: Farm managers, agricultural contractors
buyer: Farm Manager / Agricultural Contractor owner
industry: UK arable farms and contractors with precision-farming kit
current_workaround: Removing kit nightly and locking it away, CESAR marking, PIN codes, yard CCTV.
sensor_concept: Small battery tamper/motion/light sensor under the receiver mount, LoRaWAN/LTE-M with a yard gateway; alerts on removal outside working hours; evidence for the insurer.
notes: Expect strong c1 (kit value), c3 (nightly removal labour), c6 (precision-ag dealers install the GPS), c4 (insurer security recommendations); c2 risk.

title: Farm irrigation reservoirs under the Reservoirs Act need level and seepage records that are still taken by hand
problem: Large raised reservoirs (≥25,000 m³) are regulated: the undertaker must keep records of water levels and other matters and retain a supervising engineer. Missed records and inspections draw Environment Agency enforcement, and the consequences of failure are severe.
who_suffers: Farm managers acting as undertakers, supervising engineers
buyer: Farm Manager (reservoir undertaker)
industry: UK farm irrigation reservoirs registered under the Reservoirs Act 1975
current_workaround: Weekly or monthly manual level readings from a staff gauge, visual inspections, an annual supervising-engineer visit.
sensor_concept: Pressure/ultrasonic water-level sensor plus seepage flow (V-notch level) at the toe drain, LTE-M/LoRaWAN; automatic records and alerts; report for the supervising engineer.
notes: Expect strong c4 (Reservoirs Act 1975 record duties plus EA enforcement), c2 (regular readings), c3 (manual), c6 (supervising engineers and reservoir consultancies); c1 weak.

title: Hay and straw baled too damp self-heats in the barn; farmers probe stacks for weeks and fires still destroy barns
problem: Bales above ~22% moisture can self-heat over the first weeks in store. Fire services and insurers advise regular probing, yet barn fires destroy buildings, crops and machinery (~£50k-£500k) every summer.
who_suffers: Farmers, contractors, fire services
buyer: Farm Owner / Manager; forage merchant
industry: UK hay, straw and haylage production and storage
current_workaround: Manual probe thermometers pushed into stacks daily or weekly for 2-6 weeks, moisture meters at baling, stacking outdoors first.
sensor_concept: Long thermistor probe spikes left in the stack on battery LoRaWAN/LTE-M; rising-temperature alerts; post-harvest record.
notes: Expect strong c3 (manual probing), c2 (daily/weekly in season), c1 (fire costs), c6 (insurer risk surveyors, contract balers); c7 risk from existing probes.

title: Harvested field vegetables wait too long on trailers before cooling, and retailers reject or downgrade the produce
problem: Broccoli, lettuce and other field veg must reach the packhouse vacuum or hydro-cooler within tight harvest-to-cooling times set in retailer and packer specifications. Trailers left in the sun warm the produce, shortening shelf life and causing rejections or downgrades (~£2k-£10k per load).
who_suffers: Harvest crew leaders, packhouse intake QA, growers
buyer: Technical/QA Manager or Harvest Manager at a grower-packer
industry: UK field vegetable and salad grower-packers supplying multiple retailers
current_workaround: Handwritten harvest times on bin tickets, probe-thermometer checks at intake, retailer audits of harvest-to-cool records.
sensor_concept: Rugged temperature and GNSS tag on each field trailer or bin batch, LTE-M; automatic harvest-start and intake times plus pulp/air temperature; alerts when time or temperature limits approach; intake record for retailer audits.
notes: Expect strong c2 (daily in season), c3 (manual time and temperature records), c4 (retailer codes/specs and BRCGS/GLOBALG.A.P. records), c6 (packhouse QA and agronomists).

title: Pesticide spray records must log wind and weather at application, but operators guess them, and drift complaints follow
problem: Plant-protection application records under assurance schemes and the statutory code of practice should include weather conditions. Operators estimate wind, and drift onto neighbours, organic crops or water leads to complaints, regulator investigations and claims (~£ thousands), plus failed audits for incomplete records.
who_suffers: Sprayer operators, farm managers
buyer: Farm Manager / Agricultural Contractor
industry: UK arable spraying (farm-owned and contractor sprayers)
current_workaround: Handheld anemometers, Beaufort-scale guesses, paper spray records typed into farm software later, weather apps.
sensor_concept: Field-edge or sprayer-mounted anemometer and vane with temperature/RH (delta-T) and GNSS, LTE-M; attaches conditions to each spray job; alerts when wind is outside label limits.
notes: Expect strong c4 (statutory and assurance spray records), c2 (daily in spray season), c3 (manual records), c6 (agronomists and sprayer dealers); c1 drift-claim costs need sourcing; c8 anemometer cost.
